summary: R-1 follow-up from T-0763 review: ci/checks/worker-auth-public-surface.sh (FF-5, AC-19) does NOT protect src/http/router.ts from COMMITTED edits. Its router.ts branch first diffs against origin/dev (correct when reachable and un-advanced) but falls back, on ANY non-zero exit from that first diff (both 'origin/dev unreachable' AND 'origin/dev reachable and shows a real diff'), to `git diff HEAD -- router.ts` — working-tree-vs-own-HEAD, which is trivially empty for any COMMITTED change. Reproduced live: a committed router.ts edit PASSed the gate before this fix, FAILed after. Fix (a) (not (b), see rationale below): appended a new, independent, additive-only block that resolves BASE via the same merge-base fallback chain as ci/checks/agent-hire-frozen-additive.sh (FF-HIRE-4) — merge-base HEAD origin/dev -> merge-base HEAD dev -> HEAD~1 -- diffs router.ts against that BASE, and sets FAIL=1 on its own finding. FAIL is a script-global monotonic-OR variable never reset to 0 after init, so the legacy block's now-harmless vacuous OK can no longer mask the new block's real finding. The legacy block (lines 46-58) is left byte-identical and still executes -- restructuring it would require deleting/editing existing lines, which the auto_additive sanction constraint (A-1) forbids. Did NOT choose (b) (drop FF-5's router.ts branch in favor of FF-HIRE-4): FF-5 also guards 3 unrelated export invariants (DEV_USER_HEADER/registerExternalWorkerRoutes/registerAuthRoutes/createServer), and FF-HIRE-4's router.ts policy is strictly WEAKER (additive-only, permits new lines for T-0042 agent-hire routes) than FF-5's AC-19 invariant (router.ts must be fully unchanged) -- dropping FF-5's branch would silently reclassify/weaken AC-19, out of scope for an additive-only fix.

security_notes: The new authoritative check block reads only git metadata (merge-base, diff) already computed by the identical pattern in ci/checks/agent-hire-frozen-additive.sh (FF-HIRE-4) -- no new external input, no new file surface.

FAIL is a script-global bash variable initialized once to 0 and only ever assigned 1, never reset -- verified by grep across the whole file (only two 'FAIL=1' assignment sites now: the pre-existing legacy one, and the new T-0766 one). This is what makes the legacy block's continued vacuous OK harmless: it cannot un-set FAIL back to 0.

This fix does not touch src/http/router.ts, src/http/auth.ts, or any of the 4 frozen files ci/checks/agent-hire-frozen-additive.sh protects (grant-lattice.ts/grant-resolver.ts/mcp-tool-registry.ts/scoped-admin.ts) -- confirmed FF-HIRE-4 PASS, unaffected.

The auto_additive sanction is scoped to this exact {task, file} pair only (frozen-checks-immutable.sh's is_sanctioned() greps for BOTH the task and file tokens on the SAME jsonl line) -- it grants T-0766 no authority over any other frozen ci/checks/*.sh file.
follow_ups: The legacy vacuous fallback block (lines 46-58 of ci/checks/worker-auth-public-surface.sh) is now dead weight -- it still runs and can still print a misleading '[OK]... unchanged in this branch' on a real violation, even though FAIL correctly ends up set by the new block regardless. A future task with a founder-class (or a legitimately-scoped) sanction could delete/simplify it outright now that the new block is authoritative; not done here because that deletion is out of reach for an auto_additive-only thaw (A-1 forbids removing existing lines).

friction_events: worker-auth-public-surface.sh has no T-XXXX header (legacy, pre-T-0146), so frozen-checks-immutable.sh's FF-FCI11 rule ('no-header check is foreign to every task') applied and blocked the edit until an auto_additive sanction was added to ci/checks/data/frozen-sanctions.jsonl and independently verified via auto-sanction-additive.sh --verify.

auto-sanction-additive.sh's A-1 rule (every BASE_REF line, including comments, must survive byte-identical -- no deletion or in-place edit) ruled out the most direct fix (rewriting the buggy origin/dev/HEAD fallback in place to compute a correct BASE). Resolved by appending an independent new block that sets FAIL=1 on its own authoritative finding, leaving the legacy block untouched but functionally moot (FAIL is a monotonic OR, never reset).
